item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Could you add a tense instrumental bed to this cockpit clip, with no singing? I’m a little worried the music could overwhelm the radio chatter instead of supporting the tension. What I mean is, keep the entire attached 7-second clip exactly as it is visually, without changing the footage, timing, or framing. Keep the music clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks so every original word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Please keep the original radio-call recording in sync, without replacing it or adding any text. The instruments and musical style are your call.

dialog.agent:
The right approach is a sparse, tense instrumental bed—low synth pulses and restrained strings—with the music ducked beneath every radio call, especially **“Rook, you with me?”**

I can’t complete that exact mix with the connected tools: they don’t provide audio overlay or dialogue-driven ducking on an existing clip. Using video generation instead could change your footage or radio recording, so I haven’t altered the clip or spent credits.

To preserve your requirements in an editor:
- Keep the full **7-second video and original audio locked and in sync**.
- Add instrumental music on a separate track, with no vocals or text.
- Lower it during every spoken line, with extra clearance around the quoted call.
- Export by copying the original video stream, where supported, to avoid changing the footage.
dialog.why: It explicitly says the connected tools cannot overlay audio or perform dialogue-driven ducking on the existing clip, so it has not completed the mix.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

dialog.agent:
The blocker isn’t the free plan—it’s that the connected tools can’t mix music into your clip or duck it under the original radio chatter. Trying video generation could alter the footage or replace the dialogue you want preserved.

I can still make a **separate tense instrumental track**, but the music tool’s minimum length is **15 seconds**. Would you like that as a partial result, ready to trim to your 7-second clip in an editor?
dialog.why: It asks whether the user wants a separate instrumental track as a partial result and waits for their choice.
dialog.user: Yes, please go ahead and make the separate tense instrumental track as a partial result, with no singing; the instruments and style are your call. I’m still most concerned about keeping every word of the original radio calls easy to hear, especially “Rook, you with me?”

turns.agent:
The music generation was refused because your Magic Hour account has **insufficient credits**, so no track was created.

The requested 15-second instrumental costs **15 credits**. Once those are available, I can try again with sparse low synth pulses and subdued strings, without vocals or dramatic swells.

Your original clip remains untouched. The separate track would still need to be mixed and ducked beneath the radio calls to keep every word—including **“Rook, you with me?”**—clear.

approvals.name: generate_music

style.prompt: A tense but very restrained instrumental underscore for cockpit radio dialogue. Sparse soft low-register synthesizer pulses, muted low sustained strings, subtle suspenseful texture. Understated and steady from the beginning, with plenty of space for intelligible spoken radio calls. Minimal midrange activity, no lead melody, no bright high-frequency textures, no drums or sharp transients, no dramatic hits, no crescendos. Quiet background-bed character, never a foreground cue. Instrumental only, absolutely no singing, voices, spoken words, choir, or vocal samples.

That could give me clearer guidance on how to proceed with audio combinations.
